original_text:
–Reliability of Magnification Value–The magnification value given by a microscope is only valid if the size of the image is UNCHANGED.–Enlarging the image increases the magnification.–Shrinking the image reduces the magnification.–Quality images always have a scale bar; scale bar remains valid when the size of the image is changed.
2X
explanation: This slide discusses the reliability of printed or displayed magnification values. The magnification value stated by a microscope is only valid if the image size remains unchanged. Enlarging an image increases the magnification, whereas shrinking it reduces the magnification. Therefore, high-quality scientific images include a scale bar, which remains valid even when the overall size of the image is changed.

questions.q: Under what condition is the numerical magnification value printed on a microscope image no longer valid?
opts: If the size of the image is enlarged or shrunken
If the scale bar is too long
If the microscope bulb is changed
questions.exp: The slide states: 'The magnification value given by a microscope is only valid if the size of the image is UNCHANGED. Enlarging the image increases... Shrinking... reduces...'

questions.q: Why is a scale bar preferred over a simple magnification number on scientific images?
opts: It is easier to print in color.
It remains valid even when the size of the image is changed.
It shows the focal length of the objective lens.
It measures the wavelength of the illumination source.
questions.exp: The slide notes: 'scale bar remains valid when the size of the image is changed.'
